answer: Two witnesses and the midwife sign every birth in the parish birth book, and the entry names the child, the mother and the hour. A seat is given only to a name the book holds. A raven name written in at home fails the book: at the lotus of the entry the ink and the witnesses must match the midwife's own hand, and a home entry has no witnesses. Forging a birth means bribing a midwife and two witnesses, faking a delivery and paying 15,700, and the yarrow book is kept in the parish chest for a century, so a name whose birth was never witnessed is struck out.
